evidence.curator_note: Equation 9.1, UPPER branch (label 'sigma'). The page writes 'CnH2n+1 R2C-CH2R'  --(-e-)-->  CnH2n+1 R2C(+.)CH2R'  --sigma-->  CnH2n+1 R2C(+) + .CH2R''. The drawn molecular ion is SIGMA-IONIZED: the glyph between the two carbons is a '+' over a single dot printed on the C-C bond itself, i.e. a 2-centre/1-electron sigma bond, not an atom-localized radical cation. ARC COUNT (convention D): the book draws 0 curved arrows / fishhooks anywhere in Equation 9.1 - both the '-e-' ionization arrow and the 'sigma' and 'rH' branch arrows are straight, label-annotated reaction arrows, so the scheme is a net reactant->products diagram, not an arrow-pushing diagram. Both encoded electron_moves are therefore IMPLICIT (curator-reconstructed for electron balance, not drawn): move <1> puts one electron of the cleaving C2-C3 bond on C3 (giving the ethyl radical), move <2> routes the other C2-C3 electron to 'external' - the formal bookkeeping device for the EI ionization hole, because in the mapped SMILES the sigma-ionized bond is necessarily written as an ordinary 2-electron single bond while the book's bond actually holds only ONE electron; C2 is left electron-deficient -> tert-butyl cation. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are carried in the species fields against a neutral C6H14 skeleton rather than on one atom, because the book localizes '+.' on the sigma BOND (2c-1e), which has no valence-correct single-atom SMILES form; this is the same convention used for pure-hydrocarbon sigma dissociation in IMS4-EQ4.3a/b and IMS8-EQ8.37a. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the scheme is generic (n, R, R' undefined) and NO m/z and NO intensity are printed for the equation itself. Instantiated as 2,2-DIMETHYLBUTANE with n=1 (CnH2n+1 = CH3), R = R = CH3, R' = CH3 (so CH2R' = ethyl) - the smallest alkane fitting the printed skeleton in which BOTH drawn branches (this sigma branch and the rH branch of IMS9-EQ9.1b) are structurally realizable with the same precursor. Cleaving C2-C3 loses the LARGEST alkyl group (ethyl), which the citing sentence says is favored, and retains the charge at the branched carbon, giving CnH2n+1R2C+ = (CH3)3C+. observed_mz 57.0699 is the curator-computed monoisotopic value for C4H9+, NOT a measurement from this equation; page 226 does print '(CH3)3C+ (m/z 57)' - the same ion species - but it does so while discussing Figure 9.1, whose spectrum (printed on the facing page 227) is that of 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane, a different and more highly branched alkane, so detected=false and status='inferred' here and no relative_intensity is claimed.

CROSS-LINK (convention E, checked against the DFS, not assumed). rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO 9.x key at all (keys stop at 4.46 / 8.14), so no MOD rule is indexed for Equation 9.1 and no equation-keyed cross-link is asserted. Two chapter-4 rules were compared bond-for-bond against this scheme: (i) IMS_4_8 (file src/data_generation/rules/IMS_chap4_examples.py, DFS '[C+.]1([C]2(H3)(H4)(H5))([C]6(H7)(H8)(H9))([C]10(H11)(H12)(H13))[C]14(H15)(H16)[C]20(H21)(H22)(H23) >> [C+]1(three methyls) . [C.]14(H15)(H16)[C]17(H18)(H19)(H20)') encodes EXACTLY this net reaction on EXACTLY this substrate: its left side is the 2,2-dimethylbutane radical cation ionized at the quaternary carbon, it cleaves the quaternary-C-to-CH2 bond (the same bond, C2-C3 here), keeps the charge on the quaternary carbon (tert-butyl cation) and puts the radical on the departing ethyl - identical to the encoded step. Caveats, both verified by reading the source: (a) MOD localizes '+.' on an ATOM (the pipeline's ei_molecular_ion rule is '[C]1 >> [C+.]1', fires once per carbon), whereas McLafferty localizes it in the C-C sigma BOND, so the MOD reactant is a different (atom-localized) representation of the same ion; (b) IMS_4_8's DFS has an atom-identity DEFECT - the reactant's terminal methyl carbon is id 20 with hydrogens 21/22/23, while the product writes that methyl as a NEW carbon id 17 with hydrogens 18/19/20, i.e. id 20 changes element C->H, ids 17/18/19 are created and ids 21/22/23 are destroyed. Element counts (C6H14), total charge (+1) and total spin (1) still balance, so the rules/__init__.py conservation guardrail keeps the rule and MOD will still produce the correct product formulas, but the atom map is scrambled and is not usable for atom tracking. (ii) IMS_4_7 ('[C+.]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5 >> [C.]1 . [C+]2[C]3[C]4[C]5') is the generic alkane sigma-dissociation but it is the CHARGE-MIGRATION variant (charge leaves the ionized carbon, radical stays), i.e. the opposite polarization to the branch drawn here, and it additionally demands a four-carbon chain on the leaving side, so it does not describe this step. Neither rule was executed in MOD for this record; the comparison is a source-level DFS reading.
